target_customer: Data engineering and analytics teams at data-heavy companies
problem: Code changes to SQL pipelines silently broke downstream data, and teams lacked automated regression testing for data.
product_category: Data quality, data diff and migration tooling

founders.name: Gleb Mezhanskiy
founders.background_notes: YC page: built data platforms at Autodesk, Lyft and Phantom Auto. TechCrunch 2020: data scientist and engineer at Lyft, then a product manager for data tools.

founders.name: Alex Morozov
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no bio.

competitors.name: Great Expectations
competitors.what: Open source data validation with rules defined upfront
competitors.traction_then: Named in the Launch HN post as the assertion-style approach Datafold contrasts with

competitors.name: dbt tests
competitors.what: Assertion-style tests in the dbt framework
competitors.traction_then: Named in the Launch HN post as an existing alternative

technical_complexity.rationale: Value-level diffing of large tables across databases needs efficient algorithms and many connectors.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with warehouses and CI workflows add switching costs, but the company open sourced data-diff in 2022 and later sunset it in May 2024, and warehouse vendors can add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: dbt Labs partnered with Datafold in March 2022 instead of copying it; the dbt and Fivetran merger of October 2025 does not name Datafold.

market_need_then: Launch HN in August 2020 framed regression testing of ETL pipelines as a major pain point; the founder's Lyft incident where a 4-line SQL change broke data for most of a day is the origin story.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source data-diff drew a Hacker News front page post in June 2022; the project was later sunset in May 2024.

brand_strength.rationale: Data Diff is a recognised feature name and the Show HN got traction, but no evidence of brand-led growth beyond that.

pivots.from: Data diff and regression testing with open source data-diff
pivots.to: AI-powered data migration and development agents
pivots.why: Company site now emphasises migrations and AI agents; the company stopped supporting open source data-diff to focus on the commercial product.

outcome_analysis: Datafold raised a $20M Series A in November 2021 led by NEA and has stayed independent while shifting toward migration and AI agent products. It lists customers such as Disney and Databricks. Funding after the Series A is unverified, so the strength of its later growth is not shown.
notes: Co-founder name conflicts: the YC page says Alex Morozov, one profile says Alexey Astafyev. A $4M Series A-II in May 2025 appears only on CB Insights and is unverified. Total raised is $22M or $27.3M by aggregators, unverified. The Launch HN page itself returned a 503 when fetched; its content comes from search summaries. Some profiles call the batch W20, the shard and HN title say S20. Competitor traction and funding fields are null because the sources do not give them.
